decisions: Three existing story identities and all five milestone titles/routes/dates/importance/regions/calendar metadata remain. Five timeline summary strings and three library descriptions change; no new event, record, portrait or media is added. Alavara remains outside this batch.

The source’s left-path narration governs the approach despite conflicting stated intentions.

Carmen carries the limp moth boy out; that post does not name its passenger. Evrelki’s last account and Ithilrûnë’s final breath are retained without asserting an unseen completed extraction or named return. Cecil explicitly values her life while she orders him away. The ending is not turned into an all-safe victory or confirmed closure of the machine realm.

Clockwork’s source dates remain explicitly unresolved as world dates; the scene’s introductions do not silently backdate or change the separate Third Arrival canon. Brother is Evrelki’s address to Scribonia, not a new biological genealogy.

The abyssal company does not share one purpose. Damian Black remains the name used in the scene; no unconfirmed disguise identity is assigned. The pre-existing connected Magnus history/reference is retained with its scope. Alfred’s reunion/attack, Aleister’s hesitation, Velkyn’s choices and Ghilsen’s changed name/actions are distinguished.

Dumuzi’s offers, control claims and intended service remain attributed. Protected identity/origin explanations and recruitment mechanics are withheld. The narrative does not infer that he created a being merely because someone watching assumes so.

Pappy refuses an offered exit, is attacked again, and is extracted before the three remaining creatures finish the opening. His hammer splatters in the rescue energies. Creator-confirmed Cthulhu enters, consumes the creatures and leaves to serve a master. Later knowledge/consent/adjudication disputes remain separate from the actual escape and crossing.

Closing orders and discussion do not establish completed journeys or a general right to switch planes through rifts. The encounter-specific ruling is explicitly identified as governance in the evidence panel.

Babel follows departure, the salamander fight and healing, a completed teleport using the earlier beach shell, the controlled tests, cut ropes, family/rescue lures, failed extraction/restoration and the two successful interventions. Arjahn’s radiant protection is not universal; breath-holding delays exposure and Ryvyt is initially exempt because he does not breathe. No unnamed ward is assigned a spell name.

Ryvyt’s Dispel Magic frees Nymera before Scribonia’s Wish clears the wider mist. Abyss’s appearance shows continued activity after the mountain assault, not the mist’s origin or every casualty. Perceived family, Queen and children do not become independently present people, confirmed deaths or resolved family fates.

Wren’s anger after Scribonia slaps her, Arjahn’s apology and admission of continued vulnerability, Olokun’s care after needing rescue and Nymera carrying Scribonia retain distinct agency. The collapse/carry occurs after Death leaves, not before the later offer.

Dumuzi’s invocation of Oya, Aria claim and promised future stay claims; Aria’s witnessed death is not overwritten. The vision’s reception/reactions are recorded without publishing unseen video contents or protected cosmology. Refusals remain before and after it; the party leaves with exhaustion and knowledge rather than a permanent cure.
